answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to lock a bond before submitting work, then slash it when independent audits verify fraud. Audits sample claims against measurable outcomes, rather than treating popularity as proof: a violet falcon profile may look convincing, but its name earns no trust. To multiply identities, an attacker must lock real capital for each one; if caught, each fake can lose its bond, making a Sybil campaign costly, not just tedious. At the nadir of trust, the bond still gives honest participants a concrete remedy.
